*Last updated: 19 August 2026*

## Purpose and scope[^1]

[^1]: Inspired by [Stephen Senn's public declaration of interest](https://senns.uk/Declaration_Interest.htm) I decided that this should be added to my website.

This is a good-faith standing disclosure. It is intentionally broader than the competing-interest statements attached to individual publications, although it cannot capture every relationship or every way in which my judgement may be influenced. Publication-specific statements remain the most relevant source for a particular piece of research.

The organisations named here have not been asked to approve this statement. Unless I say otherwise, my publications, talks, website articles, and public comments are my own. They should not be read as statements made on behalf of an employer, client, academic institution, collaborator, or professional body, nor as evidence of that organisation's position.

Interests are context, not a substitute for engaging with an argument or analysis on its merits. Readers are nevertheless entitled to consider them when assessing my choice of questions, assumptions, interpretation, and conclusions.

## Current roles and sources of income

### MacroFactor

I am Head of Research at **MacroFactor**, a nutrition- and workouts-tracking and coaching application operated by Stronger by Science Technologies LLC. I am contracted through Steele Research Ltd. My work includes research intended to improve the evidence and models underlying nutrition and resistance-training practice. This creates a professional and financial interest in the quality, reputation, and success of MacroFactor and in research relevant to its subject matter.

### Steele Research Ltd

I am a director of **Steele Research Ltd** (also styled Steele Research Limited), through which I provide paid research consultancy. The company and I benefit professionally and financially from consultancy, commissioned research, analysis, teaching, and speaking work, and from the reputation and visibility created by my scholarly and public work.

### Kieser Australia

I provide contracted research services to **Kieser Australia** through Steele Research Ltd, having previously served as its Head of Research. Kieser provides clinical exercise and resistance-training services. This relationship is directly relevant to work involving its services, staff, members, facilities, or data, and more generally to claims about resistance training and supervised exercise.

### RMIT University

I am an **Adjunct Industry Associate Professor at RMIT University**. This is an academic affiliation without compensation and should not be taken to imply that RMIT endorses my work or views.

## Editorial, reviewing, and scholarly roles

Though I no longer hold any journal editorial positions, having stepped down from all in early 2026, I do currently serve as a recommender for **Peer Community in Health and Movement Sciences** and **Peer Community in Registered Reports**. Historical editorial and reviewing roles include:

- Editor, **Psicológica** (2023-2026);
- Editor, **International Journal of Strength and Conditioning** (2022-2026);
- Statistical Reviewer, **Sports Medicine** (from 2021);
- Managing Editor and Section Editor, **Registered Reports in Kinesiology** (2020–2022);
- Managing Editor and Section Editor, **Communications in Kinesiology** (2020–2022);
- Associate Editor for exercise physiology, **Journal of Evolution and Health** (2013-2018[^2]);
- Research Topic Editor for collections at **Frontiers in Neuroscience**, **Frontiers in Psychology**, and **Frontiers in Sports and Active Living**; and
- Guest Editor for a special issue of **BioMed Research International**.

[^2]: Though the journal website still lists me as editor it has been inactive for some time and I have not been involved in any editorial role since 2018

When I am involved in the evaluation of work through one of these roles, the relevant journal or community's procedures and any article-specific declaration should be consulted. Editorial roles may also create an interest in the standing and success of the relevant journal, community, or initiative.

I also review manuscripts, collaborate repeatedly with some researchers, and publish commentary about methods and research practice. These activities create professional relationships and prior intellectual commitments that readers may reasonably take into account.

I previously used Publons actively, subsequently incorporated into Clarivate's Web of Science, to record some of my peer-review activity. I no longer maintain the record and it may be incomplete, but the historical information remains available on my [Web of Science reviewer profile](https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/I-1944-2019). Reviewer assignments are normally confidential, so the profile may indicate journals for which I have reviewed but should not be used to infer that I reviewed a particular paper unless that review has been made public.

## Interests as a researcher, author, and consultant

My career and consultancy are helped by publishing, being read and cited, giving talks, attracting collaborators and clients, and being regarded as knowledgeable in the areas in which I work. Findings or arguments that attract attention, support earlier work, strengthen a research programme, or demonstrate the value of particular methodological expertise may benefit me even where no direct payment is involved.

I often publish with recurring collaborators and sometimes study practices or organisations with which I have worked. I may therefore have reputational interests in earlier results, theories, datasets, analytical choices, and collaborations. I try to manage these through transparent methods, open materials where possible, preregistration or Registered Reports where appropriate, and explicit study-level disclosures; none removes the interest itself.

## Intellectual commitments

I favour open, transparent, reproducible research; clear concept formation and inferential targets; explicit modelling of uncertainty; cumulative evidence synthesis; and theories capable of making precise, risky predictions. My writing is also informed by a broadly realist philosophy of science and by scepticism towards weakly specified constructs, purely procedural accounts of rigour, and claims that go beyond what a design or analysis can support.

These are intellectual positions rather than financial conflicts, but they influence the questions I consider important, the methods I prefer, and how I interpret evidence. They may also make me more receptive to work that accords with those commitments and more critical of work that does not.

## Study-specific declarations

This page does not replace the funding and competing-interest statements attached to individual papers. Those statements should identify the relationships most directly relevant to the study, including employment or contracting arrangements, organisational data or facilities, in-kind support, author roles, and editorial involvement.

My [research archive](../research/) links to publications and preprints, and my [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-8003-0757) provides an external scholarly profile.

## Corrections and omissions

I may have overlooked a relevant relationship, or a role may have changed since the date above. If you think this declaration is incomplete or inaccurate, please email [james@steele-research.com](mailto:james@steele-research.com). I will correct material errors and date substantive updates.
